Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Five-Star Business Finance 2QFY27 Earnings

I now hand the conference over to Mr. Raghav. Thank you and over to you, sir. 
Raghav: 
Good evening, everyone. On behalf of Ambit Capital, I would like to welcome you all to the 
2QFY27 Earnings Call for Five-Star Business Finance. 
Joining us from the management today, we have Mr. Lakshmipathy Deenadayalan - Chairman 
and Managing Director; Mr. Srikanth Gopalakrishnan - Joint Managing Director and CFO, and 
Mr. Prashanth Sreenivasan - Chief of Treasury and Investor Relations. 
I would like to first thank the management for giving us this opportunity to host the earnings 
call. We can now begin with the opening remarks from Mr. Lakshmipathy, post which we can 
open the floor for questions. Thank you and over to you, sir. 
 Lakshmipathy Deenadayalan:         Thank you, Raghav. Good evening, everyone. 
I am extremely happy to present to you all the details about another quarter of strong 
performance of Five-Star Business Finance. 
The quarter ended September 30, 2026, saw Five-Star delivering very strong numbers across 
various parameters. Our upward trajectory in disbursements continued during the current quarter 
as well, where we recorded our historical best disbursement of Rs. 2,078 crores, up 39% over 
previous quarter and 74% year-on-year. The loan book also saw robust growth with our AUM 
at Rs. 14,640 crores, a growth of over 6.7% over the previous quarter and 14% year-on-year. 
Importantly, this growth has come alongside improving collections and stable asset quality and 
profitability. 
Collections continue to trend very well with our unique customer collection efficiency 
improving to 98.2% in the current quarter from 97.7% in Q1, along with improvement in X-
bucket collections to 99.4% from 99.2% in Q1, which has helped contain forward flows. As a 
result, the current bucket proportion of our AUM rose sharply from 83.3% to 84.78% and 30 
plus DPD came down from 12.38% to 11.5%. With our clear focus on containing flows from 
early buckets, I am very confident that we will continue to see our portfolio quality improving 
in coming quarters.

Slippages eased marginally to 0.68% from 0.70% in Q1 and Gross Stage-3 assets were broadly 
stable at 3.48%, despite macroeconomic headwinds being witnessed across the industry. The 
credit cost improved to 1.80% of average AUM from 1.85% in Q1. We expect flattish credit 
slippages and credit cost for the rest of the year, despite the industry headwinds. Let me repeat, 
we expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of the year, despite the industry 
headwinds. With our collection framework getting better than expected results, we continue to 
focus on bringing back the growth momentum Five-Star is known for. With strong collections, 
controlled slippages and credit cost, we are well poised to continue our strong traction in 
disbursements in coming quarters, which will help us cross our growth guidance for this year 
very comfortably. 
We availed incremental debt of Rs. 825 crores during the quarter at an all-inclusive cost of 8.43% 
and our cost of funds on book eased marginally to 8.78% from 8.80% in Q1. Net interest margin 
remained broadly stable at 19.87% as against 19.97% in Q1, and was 16 bps higher year-on-
year, showing that our spreads have held up despite the drop in yields. With the tightening rate 
cycle, we expect to see some inch-up in our cost of funds, both on incremental debt and on our 
book, which would have some impact on spread and NIM. However, we expect to cushion this 
impact through yield increases on our incremental disbursements, which has been made effective 
from October 2026. Further, through the operating leverage that we will be able to achieve going 
forward, resulting from increased productivity, higher growth, tighter control over operational 
and credit cost, we are confident of largely offsetting the hawkish stance of RBI expected for 
the next few quarters. 
On the profitability side, we clocked a PAT of Rs. 299 crores for the quarter, up 10% sequentially 
and 5% year-on-year. This includes a one-time tax benefit of Rs. 19 crores pertaining to previous 
years. Even excluding this, our PAT was 3% higher on a sequential basis. We have seen 
improvements to return ratios compared to the previous quarter. ROA was up 28 bps to 8.39%, 
and ROE up 79 bps to 15.25%. For the first half of this year, we have clocked a PAT of Rs. 571 
crores, up 3% year-on-year. 
After a year beset with challenges across multiple fronts, we have bounced back stronger than 
before. Some of these numbers across disbursements and collections are our historical best and 
clearly validate the actions we have taken over the last few quarters. They have also strengthened 
our confidence that we are moving in the right direction of onwards and upwards. 
Let me hand it over to Srikanth for further details.

last couple of years being beset with multiple challenges facing the company as well as the 
industry, with all the metrics stacking up very well across various parameters. Alongside our

unavailed sanctions of about Rs. 1,100 crores, which is more than sufficient for us to take care 
of our requirements over the next quarter. As was stated in the opening remarks by Mr. Pathy, 
we should expect some compression in spreads given the tightening interest rate cycle, but the 
increase in yields on incremental lending should help cushion this. 
On the DPDs, we are very glad to inform all of you that our DPDs improved significantly, with 
1+ dropping from 16.7% to 15.2%, and 30 plus dropping to 11.5% from 12.38%. Even in terms

being that with the disbursement momentum back, the collections holding up extremely well, 
we are poised to cross our growth guidance for this year in a very comfortable way. 
On that positive note, we will take a pause here and happy to invite any questions from any of 
you. Thank you.
